models.name: Inflow-RANS
models.what_it_computes: Steady Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes solution with SST k–ω closure and non-Newtonian blood rheology to predict wall shear stress fields, Eulerian scalar residence time, and an Eulerian platelet activation index in the near-inflow region.

models.name: Inflow-LES-PaRT
models.what_it_computes: Wall-resolved large-eddy simulation with Lagrangian platelet surrogate particles to compute stress-exposure histories, residence time distributions, and near-wall deposition propensity at the inflow.

mechanisms.name: High-shear platelet activation
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Localized acceleration at the cannula lip and within the inlet housing can expose platelets to supraphysiologic shear, priming them for activation.

mechanisms.name: Recirculation-driven stasis
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Separated flow and vortical structures adjacent to the inflow can increase residence time, promoting coagulation cascade initiation.

mechanisms.name: Surface-mediated deposition
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Sustained low wall shear near biomaterial surfaces at the inflow facilitates adhesion and growth of thrombus.

deviation.detail: All credibility factors are scored on a 0–12 numeric scale for each model–mechanism pair, and an overall credibility index is reported on the same 0–12 scale.

expected_decision.outcome_source: The steady RANS model with SST closure and non-Newtonian rheology is credible for localizing and ranking high-shear hotspots that condition platelet activation, with quantitative agreement to bench WSS metrics within approximately 20 percent RMSE and moderate sensitivity to mesh refinement.

datasets: transparent, index-matched mock loop reproducing the inflow geometry and physiologic impedance
Particle image velocimetry (PIV) provided planar velocity fields
dye washout T90 concentration decay in interrogation regions
fluorescent platelet deposition fields imaged by confocal microscopy

name_keywords: dye washout T90 and KS distance
dye washout T90 and KS distance

expected_context_of_use: The questions the models are expected to inform are: (a) where and by how much do shear stresses near the cannula lip and inlet housing exceed relevant thresholds for platelet activation over clinically relevant ranges of operating conditions; (b) what is the extent and strength of recirculation zones that could produce stasis adjacent to the inflow; and (c) which surfaces and locations present sustained low-shear and high near-wall residence time that predispose to surface deposition.

spans: For Inflow-RANS, the SST closure with shear-thinning viscosity aligned reasonably with the need to localize shear hotspots: the peak WSS along the lip and the leading inner edge of the bell-mouth are geometry-driven, and the mean stress field positions these reliably.

For high-shear activation questions centered on where the peak wall shear stress occurs and its approximate magnitude at design points, the SST model generally performs well, particularly when the geometry-induced acceleration is strong and dominant over turbulence fluctuations.

spans: A quasi-steady viewpoint cannot capture cyclic reattachment and vortex shedding.
As a result, pathlines through low-speed regions miss variability important for the stasis question.
findings.span: A quasi-steady viewpoint cannot capture cyclic reattachment and vortex shedding.

spans: For surface precipitation, the steady field does not provide a time-resolved picture of low-shear persistence.

For surface-mediated deposition questions that hinge on low-shear persistence and near-wall transport, steady models omit the fluctuations that can periodically disrupt low-shear zones, thereby potentially under- or over-predicting the persistence depending on bias in the computed mean field.
findings.span: For surface precipitation, the steady field does not provide a time-resolved picture of low-shear persistence.

spans: In the high-shear regime, the temporal dynamics of acceleration and deceleration phases are resolved, and the particle stress histories span the relevant range from 2 to 200 Pa*s per cycle near the lip in the 4.5 L/min condition.

By eliminating a wall model and achieving y-plus below one, the simulation can represent the time-varying wall shear stress in acceleration and deceleration phases and resolve coherent vortical structures that govern entrainment into and out of recirculation zones.
findings.span: In the high-shear regime, the temporal dynamics of acceleration and deceleration phases are resolved, and the particle stress histories span the relevant range from 2 to 200 Pa*s per cycle near the lip in the 4.5 L/min condition.

spans: For stasis, coherent vortical structures adjacent to the bell-mouth are resolved, and their entrainment of particles into and out of the near-wall low-speed zones is captured.
findings.span: For stasis, coherent vortical structures adjacent to the bell-mouth are resolved, and their entrainment of particles into and out of the near-wall low-speed zones is captured.

spans: For deposition, the use of a combined shear–time criterion for near-wall persistence provides an interpretable surrogate for adhesive stabilization, though the absence of explicit receptor kinetics remains a limitation.

For surface-mediated deposition, the inclusion of a persistent low-shear criterion in the near-wall region provides a more direct surrogate for adhesive stabilization than instantaneous shear thresholds alone.
findings.span: For deposition, the use of a combined shear–time criterion for near-wall persistence provides an interpretable surrogate for adhesive stabilization, though the absence of explicit receptor kinetics remains a limitation.
